title: SLO Stewardship Activation Briefing
content:
Purpose
-----
Rapid, executable plan to activate SLO stewardship across product and infra teams for the winter rollout window. This brief focuses on how we (SRE) will shift from advisory -> operational ownership for selected critical SLOs, including a lightweight "Responsibility Roulette" to make handoffs explicit and short-lived.

Scope and goals
---------------
- Scope: customer-facing inference API paths (text-generation, chat streaming, embeddings) + control plane (auth/quotas). Excludes telemetry pipeline changes (separate track).
- Goals (30/60/90):
  - 30d: finalize SLO definitions, alert-to-owner mapping, and error-budget spend policy for each product area.
  - 60d: run two mini-canary rollouts with automatic fallback and measure alert noise reduction by 30%.
  - 90d: establish continuous SLO steward rotation, update runbooks, and integrate SLO dashboards into Console-weekly reports.

Principles
----------
1) Lightweight, reversible changes only during activation window.
2) SLOs should map to a single measurable signal where possible (p95 latency, success rate, tail errors).
3) Keep ownership explicit — no ambiguous escalation paths.
4) Automate guardrails (auto-fallback, throttles) before changing alert thresholds.

Concrete deliverables (by team)
--------------------------------
- SRE (owner: Priya Kapoor):
  - Deliver SLO definitions doc with measurement queries and tags. (due 2026-12-10)
  - Implement alert routing rules in PagerDuty for new SLOs. (due 2026-12-17)
  - Ship canary runbook and rollback checklist. (due 2026-12-20)
- Platform (owner: Ethan Liu):
  - Expose SLO-friendly metrics in telemetry (per-route latency histograms, success codes) and ensure retention 90d. (due 2026-12-15)
  - Add tag metadata to traces to map to ownership. (due 2027-01-05)
- Product (owner: Ava Park):
  - Sign off SLO targets and customer impact statements. (due 2026-12-08)
  - Prepare feature gating for canary traffic splits. (due 2026-12-18)
- Observability (owner: Miguel Santos):
  - Create dashboards and anomaly detection alerts for each SLO. (due 2026-12-17)
  - Publish daily health report template for stakeholders. (due 2026-12-22)
- Solutions/Support (owner: Sofia Martinez):
  - Draft customer-facing incident guidance and communication templates tied to SLO breaches. (due 2026-12-12)

Activation cadence (week-by-week snapshot)
-----------------------------------------
- Week 0 (Nov 23 - Nov 29): Kickoff, gather product signoffs, verify metrics availability.
- Week 1 (Nov 30 - Dec 6): Finalize SLO language and owners; SRE publishes initial measurement queries.
- Week 2 (Dec 7 - Dec 13): Platform and Observability complete data plumbing; Product approves targets.
- Week 3 (Dec 14 - Dec 20): Run small canary (5% traffic) for inference-api with SLO monitoring; collect signals.
- Week 4 (Dec 21 - Dec 27): Retro canary; roll forward to 20% if safe; update runbooks and PD escalation.
- Jan (follow-up): Rotate stewardship, integrate into Console dashboards, begin monthly SLO reviews.

Responsibility Roulette (how rotation works)
-------------------------------------------
- Pattern: 2-week steward shifts. Each steward owns the SLO scorecard, triage coordination, and single-point escalation for their window.
- Roster (first cycle): Priya (week A), Ethan (week B), Ava (week C), Miguel (week D).
- Handoff process: edit live steward card, quick huddle (10m), and update runbook notes.

Alerting and error budget policy (high level)
-------------------------------------------
- Alert tiers:
  - P0: service-wide outage affecting >5% customers or API 500 spikes. Immediate page.
  - P1: SLO burn rate >3x sustained for 15m. Page steward.
  - P2: Incremental error spikes or latency regressions affecting internal tests. Slack alert.
- Error budget consumption rules:
  - If 50% of monthly budget spent in first 10 days -> stop all non-essential deploys for that service and triage.
  - If 90% spent -> require cross-functional review and customer comms plan.

Runbook changes and docs
------------------------
- Minimal runbook template will be pushed to Confluence and linked in PD incidents. Key sections: SLO definition, measurement query, alert mapping, rollback steps, customer impact blurb, contact roster.
- Ownership of runbook updates: whoever makes a change to the service must update the runbook before merging related code (enforced via PR checklist).

Risk & mitigations
------------------
- Risk: telemetry gaps discovered during canary -> Mitigation: fallback to synthetic probes and extend canary window.
- Risk: alert fatigue from noisy SLO signals -> Mitigation: tune thresholds in staging and require two-stage alerts (investigate -> page).
- Risk: cross-team coordination lag over holidays -> Mitigation: schedule critical steps before Dec 20 and keep a small on-call overlap during holiday week.

Decision log (open items)
------------------------
1) Should we include control plane auth latency in the same SLO as inference path? (Decision owner: Product; linked JIRA REL-4623)
2) Do we allow teams to apply per-service exemptions for 2-week maintenance windows without consuming error budget? (Owner: SRE and Legal)
3) Final burn rate thresholds for P1/P2 alerts (Owner: Observability).

Communication plan
------------------
- Weekly digest to stakeholders (product, sales engineering, success) with: SLO health snapshot, top incidents, action items.
- Immediate comms: If monthly error budget projected to exceed 75%, Solutions will craft a customer note for impacted accounts.

Success metrics (how we know activation worked)
---------------------------------------------
- Technical: reduction in noisy pages by >=30% within 60d; error budget consumption aligned with historical incident rates; dashboards reporting reliable SLO scores (no NaNs) 99% of the time.
- Organizational: 90% of teams adopt steward rotation and update runbooks in PRs; time-to-diagnosis for SLO-related pages reduced by 25%.

Post-activation review and cadence
--------------------------------
- 30-day retro after primary rollout: collect incident/op metrics, steward feedback, and suggested improvements.
- Monthly SLO health reviews for the first 6 months, then quarterly once stable.

Quick to-dos (today)
--------------------
- Priya: finish SLO definitions doc and share with Product for signoff.
- Ethan: validate metric tags availability and respond to REL-4623 follow-ups.
- Miguel: create skeleton dashboards and invite stakeholders.
- Ava: confirm feature gating timeline with platform.

Notes to self
------------
- Keep changes reversible and minimize config sprawl.
- Document any temporary exceptions with expiration dates.
- Expect several small adjustments after the first canary; plan time for follow-up sprints.

References and links
--------------------
- Confluence: SRE SLO framework (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: REL-4623 (SLO definition debate)
- GitHub: infra-config changes for PagerDuty routing

End of briefing.
